queue_items.claim: The row's only close warrant is an original-language formula claim asserted with no pointed splice and keyed to the translation witness.
queue_items.grounds: boundary_rationale closes: the unit 'closes two verses later on ... (web:Isa.43.15), just ahead of the second fresh koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.43.16.' Nothing else supports the close. The frame is boundary-relevant original-language content and ships unspliced under a web: ref, against the mandatory engagement class. Checked against the bytes the claim is true: MT 43:16 opens כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ (oshb:Isa.43.16, tier: byte), one of only 4 koh-amar verses in chs 41-43 (MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16). The seam is sound; the warrant as shipped is not evidenced to standard.
queue_items.proposed_change: Splice the koh-amar onset at oshb:Isa.43.16 with its tier named as the close warrant, alongside the existing web: reference.

queue_items.claim: The strongest-rejected-alternative field records only the rival's own supporting reasons and no ground for rejecting it, on a rival that would merge this span away.
queue_items.grounds: The field reads: 'A rival reading keeps this two-verse Redeemer announcement joined to the new-thing oracle that follows as one Babylon-and-exodus complex, since both open on a Yahweh...says pattern and share the redemption theme.' The since-clause argues for the rival; no counter is recorded. Adopting the rival would merge Isa.43.14-Isa.43.15 into the following unit, so the gap is span-relevant. The ground that defeats it exists in the bytes and is not stated in the field: MT 43:16 opens its own frame, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.16, tier: byte), and MT 43:14 opens another, so two frames stand where the rival sees one complex.
queue_items.proposed_change: Record the refusal in the field: two distinct koh-amar frames stand at oshb:Isa.43.14 and oshb:Isa.43.16, which is what separates the two units rather than joining them.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar frame opens the row at “Yahweh, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says:” (web:Isa.43.14), the full title stack spliced at כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.43.14, byte tier) -- a different divine-title pairing than the witness-trial's bare self-declaration at web:Isa.43.11-Isa.43.13. The oracle announces “For your sake, I have sent to Babylon” and closes two verses later on “I am Yahweh, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.” (web:Isa.43.15), just ahead of the second fresh koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.43.16.

shipped_row.device_notes: The oracle announces judgment on Babylon and the Chaldeans, but its address and rhetorical purpose comfort Israel (‘for your sake’), so the row reads it under the salvation-oracle default rather than as a judgment oracle against a third party; the rival merged reading is disclosed above.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A byte-visible participant shift opens the row: the first-person divine speech that closes Isa.43.7 gives way to a directive naming a third party, הוֹצִ֥יא עַם עִוֵּ֖ר (oshb:Isa.43.8, byte tier) -- a directive reading, since no per-token parsing layer is staged to fix an imperative or vocative shape at this verse -- “Bring out the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears.” (oshb:Isa.43.8), turning into the nations-summons כָּֽל הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו (oshb:Isa.43.9, byte tier), “Let all the nations be gathered together...Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified” (oshb:Isa.43.9) and the courtroom verdict “"You are my witnesses," says Yahweh” (oshb:Isa.43.10), spliced at אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.10, byte tier). The same verse also names “my servant whom I have chosen” (web:Isa.43.10) in the same breath as the witness verdict; the byte census leaves that servant figure unnamed here, so the row treats the phrase as the addressed ‘you’ of the witness clause rather than deciding it is Israel. The self-declaration “I myself am Yahweh. Besides me, there is no savior.” (web:Isa.43.11) carries through to the close “Yes, since the day was, I am he.” (web:Isa.43.13), spliced at גַּם מִיּוֹם֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.43.13, byte tier), ahead of the fresh koh-amar frame naming the Redeemer at web:Isa.43.14.

queue_items.claim: The row's back-seam warrant names a fear-not formula as the onset signal at web:Isa.44.1, but no fear-not formula stands in that verse's bytes in either witness.
queue_items.grounds: The shipped prose reads 'just ahead of the fresh fear-not address to “Jacob my servant” that opens web:Isa.44.1'. MT 44:1 in full is וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier), whose onset run is וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier) — an adversative plus imperative — and WEB 44:1 reads “Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.” (web:Isa.44.1). The fear-not formula stands one verse later: אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.44.2, byte tier), a pair re-collated here as byte-identical to the fear-not opening the address at oshb:Isa.43.1 (byte tier). The book-order neighbour row argues this same seam incompatibly, stating that the divine frame and the fear-not it governs stand one verse inside its unit rather than at its onset, so the two rows locate one formula at two different verses. The named-servant half of the descriptor is byte-true at 44:1, and the seam itself survives on the adversative-plus-imperative onset, on the closing verdict at web:Isa.43.28 and on the disclosed SAMEKH at MT 43:28, so the defect lies in the stated warrant rather than in the cut.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: replace 'the fresh fear-not address ... that opens web:Isa.44.1' with the onset signal actually standing in that verse — the adversative-plus-imperative וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier) with its named-servant address — and, if the fear-not is cited at all, locate it at oshb:Isa.44.2 with web:Isa.44.2 added to boundary_evidence_refs.

Declare your case, that you may be justified.” (web:Isa.43.26) carries the indictment through to the verdict “Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult.” (web:Isa.43.28), just ahead of the fresh fear-not address to “Jacob my servant” that opens web:Isa.44.1.

queue_items.claim: The row's cross-seam catchword disclosure labels the two witness forms as matching at skeleton tier only, but they are not identical at skeleton tier.
queue_items.grounds: The two spliced runs are וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) and וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier). Their skeletons, taken from the staged consonantal layer, are distinct strings, and so are the skeletons of the two witness tokens alone — עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) against וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier). The relation is root sharing with containment of the shorter skeleton inside the longer, not skeleton-tier identity; the row's own added clause about sharing the same witness root states the true relation, and the tier label then overstates it. The book-order neighbour rows state the structurally identical redeemer catchword correctly, as sharing a root in different conjugations and not identical at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair to device_notes: strike 'and matching at skeleton tier only', state the relation as root-level with containment of the shorter skeleton, and add skeleton to the existing non-identity list alongside byte, nfd and accent-stripped.

queue_items.claim: The row disambiguates the rock epithet against the adversary and Tyre homographs 'sharing its skeleton', but neither shares that skeleton, and the claim ships without a digit or a named count object.
queue_items.grounds: The row's own splice is צ֖וּר (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier). Tyre stands as צֹ֑ר (oshb:Isa.23.1, byte tier) at the head of its own oracle, and its two-consonant skeleton is not a contiguous substring of the rock epithet's three-consonant skeleton; the adversary and narrow family carries that same two-consonant skeleton. A word-unbound contiguous skeleton sweep on the rock epithet's consonants returns 23 verses (sweep: 23 verses; count object: skeleton substring), and the chapter-23 Tyre oracle verses are absent from that list. The verses that genuinely share the skeleton are the besieged, fortified, reaping and refining families — for example נְצוּרָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.8, byte tier) and מָצ֑וֹר (oshb:Isa.19.6, byte tier) — alongside the rock-epithet sites themselves. The disambiguation therefore names two classes that are not skeleton-sharers and omits the class that is.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: either drop the homograph clause, or restate it against the classes that actually share the epithet's skeleton with a digit and count object named, keeping the Tyre and adversary contrast only if labelled a pointed-form contrast rather than a skeleton one.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The unit shifts at “Everyone who makes a carved image is vain.” (web:Isa.44.9), spliced at יֹֽצְרֵי פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.44.9, byte tier) against the preceding verse's first-person divine speech to a plural addressee, הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.8, byte tier) -- a byte-visible participant shift in which both the divine speaker and the addressed 'you' drop out, replaced by third-person description; no divine first person stands anywhere in Isa.44.9-Isa.44.20, and the span's first-person forms -- four sites, web:Isa.44.16, web:Isa.44.17, web:Isa.44.19, web:Isa.44.20 -- sit inside the idol-maker's own quoted or reported speech. No koh-amar or fear-not frame interrupts the workman-by-workman description (blacksmith, carpenter, tree-planter) through to the self-indictment “Isn't there a lie in my right hand?” (web:Isa.44.20); the idol-maker's own plea, “and prays to it, and says, "Deliver me, for you are my god!"”, sits inside this span at web:Isa.44.17, one of the row's ketiv/qere verses (K/Q), and the same span carries the small-nun seg that is the book's only special letter (sweep: 1 seg across 1,291 MT verses) at oshb:Isa.44.14 (single-witness; the row makes no claim about its position within the verse). The row's closing verse sits just ahead of the exhortation that opens web:Isa.44.21.

A forming-root chain runs across both of the row's own seams at skeleton tier: יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י (oshb:Isa.43.21) before the unit and יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד לִי֙ (oshb:Isa.44.21) after it frame the span, matched inside it by the row's own onset יֹֽצְרֵי (oshb:Isa.44.9) and by the satire's own workmen at יָצַ֥ר אֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.44.10) and יִצְּרֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.44.12), with וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן (oshb:Isa.44.2) a further instance just beyond the front seam -- nine verses across chapters 43-44 carry the contiguous forming skeleton, with no plene spelling attested in that window.

queue_items.claim: The row states the location and direction of its tier-3 parashah evidence backwards: the petuchah falls on the row's own closing seam and separates the section from the following oracle, rather than sitting on the far side of that seam and grouping the section with it.
queue_items.grounds: The mark inventory (WLC single witness, MT keys) carries SAMEKH at MT 44:20 and PE at MT 44:23, so the section those marks bound is MT 44:21-44:23 and the PE closes it after 44:23. The row's span is the single verse Isa.44.23-Isa.44.23, whose closing seam is 44:23|44:24 — exactly where that PE falls, not on its far side; and a section end after 44:23 divides 44:21-44:23 from the koh-amar oracle spliced at כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier) rather than grouping them with it. The layer's real direction is weak corroboration of the row's closing seam together with pressure against its front seam at 44:22|44:23, which is the row's own disclosed rival; the shipped sentence reverses both. The immediately preceding book-order row describes the same section correctly, as running Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 and grouping its span with the following doxology, so the two rows give incompatible accounts of one mark. The cut is unaffected: the row rests it on the addressee turn at רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי עָשָׂ֣ה (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier) and expressly not on the tier-3 layer.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale: restate the mark as a petuchah closing the MT 44:21-44:23 section at the row's own closing seam, weak tier-3 corroboration of that seam, while grouping the row's verse with the exhortation before it and so running against the row's front seam; retain the existing disclaimer that the cut rests on the addressee turn.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The single verse “Sing, you heavens, for Yahweh has done it! Shout, you lower parts of the earth! Break out into singing, you mountains, O forest, all of your trees, for Yahweh has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel.” (web:Isa.44.23) is an imperative hymn call to the cosmos, spliced at רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier), set apart from the exhortation before it by its shift from second-person address (‘you are my servant’) to an imperative summons of heavens, earth, and mountains -- a doxology-closure unit for the redemption announcement that precedes it, standing just ahead of the fresh koh-amar self-predication that opens web:Isa.44.24. The petuchah after this verse (oshb:Isa.44.23, single-witness, tier-3) closes the layer's section on the FAR side of the row's own closing seam, grouping Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 with the koh-amar oracle that follows rather than corroborating the isolation argued here; the cut itself rests on the addressee turn, not on that tier-3 layer.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading merges this doxology into the exhortation of Isa.44.21-Isa.44.22 as its closing acclamation rather than isolating it as its own hymn row.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: one-verse doxology closing the redemption announcement

shipped_row.device_notes: The verse is held as its own isolable doxology-closure unit on the strength of its imperative cosmic-summons form, distinct from both the second-person exhortation before it and the koh-amar self-predication after it. A redeemer catchword straddles both of the row's own seams at root/skeleton level, not as a byte-identical refrain: כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22, byte tier) before it, the row's own כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier), and גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier, the quoted token standing clear of that verse's ketiv/qere token pair, single-witness apparatus) after it -- a device that argues continuity across both seams without disturbing the cut, which rests on the addressee turn.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The address returns to direct exhortation at “Remember these things, Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant.” (web:Isa.44.21), spliced at זְכָר אֵ֣לֶּה יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י עַבְדִּי אָ֑תָּה (oshb:Isa.44.21, byte tier) -- Jacob and Israel again NAMED as servant, echoing Isa.44.1-Isa.44.2 rather than the unnamed servant-figure class. The blotted-transgression announcement closes at “Return to me, for I have redeemed you.” (oshb:Isa.44.22), and the row's own final verse sits just before the heavens' song that opens oshb:Isa.44.23, where a petuchah closes the layer's section (oshb:Isa.44.23, single-witness, tier-3); that section runs Isa.44.21-Isa.44.23 and so groups the row's span with the following doxology that the disclosed rival would absorb, rather than corroborating the row's own cut, which rests on the tier-1 return-address change at Isa.44.21, not on the tier-3 layer.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading keeps the heavens' doxology of Isa.44.23 inside this same unit as its closing acclamation rather than granting it a separate hymn row, since its opening ‘for Yahweh has redeemed Jacob’ directly answers this row's own ‘I have redeemed you.’

prev_row.device_notes: The redemption vocabulary at the close of this row (‘I have redeemed you’) recurs immediately in the doxology that follows (‘Yahweh has redeemed Jacob’) as a root-level catchword rather than a repeated form: כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ (oshb:Isa.44.22, byte tier) against כִּֽי גָאַ֤ל (oshb:Isa.44.23, byte tier) share the same redemption root in different conjugations, not identical at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier; the row discloses that catchword pull toward the next unit rather than absorbing the doxology into its own span.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar frame opens the row at “Yahweh, your Redeemer, and he who formed you from the womb says: “I am Yahweh, who makes all things” (web:Isa.44.24), spliced at כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן (oshb:Isa.44.24, byte tier; this is the row's only ketiv/qere site, K/Q). The participle chain runs unbroken through “who says of Jerusalem, 'She will be inhabited;'” (web:Isa.44.26) to the naming of Cyrus, “who says of Cyrus, 'He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure,'” (web:Isa.44.28), spliced at הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֨וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י (oshb:Isa.44.28, byte tier) -- one of the book's two sites naming Cyrus by name -- just ahead of the second, separately framed koh-amar oracle addressed directly to Cyrus that opens web:Isa.45.1.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading carries this self-predication straight through the Cyrus commission that follows as one oracle without a fresh koh-amar break, since both share the same divine-maker vocabulary and the Cyrus figure named at the end of this row is addressed directly in the next.

queue_items.claim: The row holds two independently-marked woe onsets as one unit at confidence high while a span-internal section mark stands at exactly the disclosed rival's split point, and the prose nowhere discloses that the tier-3 layer runs against the merge.
queue_items.grounds: The row's own two splices are ה֗וֹי רָ֚ב אֶת יֹ֣צְר֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.9, byte tier) and ה֛וֹי אֹמֵ֥ר לְאָ֖ב (oshb:Isa.45.10, byte tier), and the book's device spine lists MT 45:9 and MT 45:10 as two separate verse-initial woe-oracle onsets rather than one, so the rival the row discloses rests on a tier-1 signal at 45:10 and not merely on repetition. The mark inventory (WLC single witness, MT keys) additionally carries SAMEKH at MT 45:9: a section end falling inside the row's own span, at precisely the 45:9|45:10 split the rival proposes, with further SAMEKH at MT 45:8 and MT 45:10 leaving each woe standing as its own section in that layer. The row lists all three marks in boundary_evidence_refs but its prose engages none of them and it asserts confidence high. The immediately preceding book-order row meets the structurally identical situation, a SAMEKH at MT 45:7 backing its own isolate-the-closing-verse rival, by holding confidence at medium with the frontier flag set, so the calibration is inconsistent within the run. Tier-3 is never a boundary driver here and the merge remains a legitimate disclosed reading, so this is a calibration and disclosure defect, not a demonstrated boundary error.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair: disclose in device_notes that the parashah layer divides the pair at the row's internal 45:9|45:10 point and so argues for the disclosed rival, and step confidence from high to medium with frontier_flag_considered set true, matching the neighbour row's handling of the same situation. No respan proposed.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A paired hoy onset opens the row at “Woe to him who strives with his Maker- a clay pot among the clay pots of the earth!” (web:Isa.45.9), spliced at ה֗וֹי רָ֚ב אֶת יֹ֣צְר֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.9, byte tier), matched immediately by the second woe “Woe to him who says to a father, 'What have you become the father of?'” (web:Isa.45.10), spliced at ה֛וֹי אֹמֵ֥ר לְאָ֖ב (oshb:Isa.45.10, byte tier) -- two verse-initial hoy onsets read as one twinned unit rather than split into separate woes, just ahead of the koh-amar reply that opens web:Isa.45.11.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading splits the potter-clay woe of Isa.45.9 from the parent-child woe of Isa.45.10 as two separate one-verse units, since each opens on its own hoy exclamation.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A second, distinct koh-amar frame opens the row at “Yahweh says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held” (web:Isa.45.1), spliced at כֹּה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ לִמְשִׁיחוֹ֮ לְכ֣וֹרֶשׁ (oshb:Isa.45.1, byte tier) -- Cyrus's other named site in the book, a fresh verse-initial messenger formula naming its own addressee, distinct from the participle standing inside the frame-chain at oshb:Isa.44.28. Direct second-person address itself opens one verse later, אֲנִי֙ לְפָנֶ֣יךָ אֵלֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.45.2, byte tier). The commission runs through the purpose clause “that you may know that it is I, Yahweh, who calls you by your name” (web:Isa.45.3) and the naming עַבְדִּ֣י יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּחִירִ֑י (oshb:Isa.45.4, byte tier), “For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel my chosen” (web:Isa.45.4) -- Jacob named servant, Israel named chosen -- to the exclusive-deity formula “I am Yahweh, and there is no one else.” (web:Isa.45.6). One of the row's verses, web:Isa.45.2, is a ketiv/qere site (K/Q). The row closes on the heavens-and-earth imperative “Rain, you heavens, from above...I, Yahweh, have created it.” (web:Isa.45.8), just ahead of the paired hoy onset that opens web:Isa.45.9.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading isolates the closing rain-and-righteousness call of Isa.45.8 as its own short doxology-closure unit, on the model of Isa.44.23's imperative summons to heavens and earth, rather than holding it inside the Cyrus commission.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar frame answers the woe pair at “Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel and his Maker says:” (web:Isa.45.11), spliced at כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְיֹצְר֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.45.11, byte tier), turning the potter-clay challenge into the article-marked object הָאֹתִיּ֣וֹת שְׁאָל֔וּנִי (oshb:Isa.45.11, byte tier) followed by the summons תְּצַוֻּֽנִי (oshb:Isa.45.11, byte tier) -- a prefix-conjugation form carrying the same first-person object suffix as the summons before it -- with no interrogative particle or pronoun standing anywhere in the verse, unlike the genuine interrogative he opening the woe pair itself, הֲיֹאמַ֨ר (oshb:Isa.45.9, byte tier). “You ask me about the things that are to come, concerning my sons, and you command me concerning the work of my hands!” (web:Isa.45.11) The unit closes on the unnamed ‘he’ who “He shall build my city, and he shall let my exiles go free” (web:Isa.45.13), a Cyrus-recalling promise without naming him again, just ahead of the next koh-amar frame that opens web:Isa.45.14.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading classes this unit as a salvation oracle rather than a trial speech, on the strength of its closing city-building and exile-release promise, since the disputation frame is brief and gives way quickly to restoration language.
next_row.literature_type_guess: disputation answering the potter-clay challenge, closing on renewed commission language

next_row.device_notes: The row is argued as trial_speech on its summons-and-command shape (the article-marked object followed by the paired first-person-suffixed verbs, ‘you command me concerning the work of my hands’) rather than a question form; no morphology layer is staged to fix whether the summons form carries imperative or indicative force, so that reading is held open. The salvation-oracle rival is disclosed above and the choice between the two is held loosely.
